chunk_findings.detail: `_ReplyFile` stamps `run_token` from the process-global `_RUN`, which the next `review()` overwrites, so files are not owned by the invocation that will look them up. Given thread A calling `_begin_run("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")` and then creating its reply file only after thread B's `_begin_run("2026-01-01T00:00:01Z")`, that file is stored with `run_token [REDACTED] "2026-01-01T00:00:01Z"`. A's kill path calls `active_files(item, gate, "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")` and gets `[]`, so `_terminated_gate` records `unavailable` and drops the checkpointed chunks. The same mis-tag happens on a nested `review()` in one thread. The new test only constructs the file before the second `_begin_run`, so it never catches this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/reviewers.py:_begin_run

chunk_findings.detail: `_ACTIVE` is appended to with no lock while `active_files` iterates it, and `_begin_run` no longer isolates runs. A sibling `review()` constructing a `_ReplyFile` during `_terminated_gate`'s `for f in _ACTIVE` raises `RuntimeError` (list size changed). That exception is not caught at the call site in `gate.py`, so the SIGTERM path aborts before writing the partial gate record.

chunk_findings.detail: `_begin_run` now does `_ACTIVE.clear()`, and `active_files` no longer scopes by invocation, so a second `review()` in the same process (the MCP worker this comment says can host a review) drops the first run's reply files. Given run A checkpointing chunk 1 on item/gate, then run B entering `review()` so `_begin_run` clears `_ACTIVE` before B appends its own file: A's SIGTERM path calls `active_files(item, gate)` and gets `[]` (or B's chunks if B reused the same item and gate), so `_terminated_gate` records `unavailable` / "nothing reviewed" instead of A's partial findings — the loss bug B982d306cc8 claims to fix. The same `clear()` during A's `for f in _ACTIVE` raises `RuntimeError` before the gate record is written. The regression test that asserted a later `_begin_run` must not drop a sibling file is deleted in this diff.
